cases.description: When the JSON document (rootNode) is null the method should immediately throw a NullPointerException because validation cannot be performed on a non‑existent node.
When the OutputFormat instance is null the method should reject the call with an IllegalArgumentException, as it has no way to produce a result.

A JSON document that conforms to the schema should result in an empty set of ValidationMessage objects. The mock OutputFormat receives this empty set and returns a predefined success value (outputSuccess).
A JSON document that violates the schema generates one or more ValidationMessage objects. The mock OutputFormat collects those messages and returns a predefined failure value (outputFailure).
If the OutputFormat implementation throws a RuntimeException while processing the validation result, the validate method should propagate that exception unchanged.

When a non‑null ExecutionContextCustomizer is supplied (via the overload that eventually calls this method), it may modify the ExecutionContext (e.g., enable/disable certain validators). The test verifies that the customizer is invoked and that validation still succeeds, returning the customizer‑aware output.

When the supplied JsonNode is a Jackson MissingNode (represents a non‑existent JSON value) the validator should treat it as a valid instance for an empty schema and forward an empty ValidationMessage set to the OutputFormat, which returns the predefined success value.

group: RootNode is JSON null with required type mismatch

cases.description: The schema requires a non‑null type (e.g., "type": "object"). Providing a JsonNode that represents JSON null should generate a ValidationMessage about type mismatch, which the mock OutputFormat collects and returns the predefined failure value.
If the OutputFormat implementation returns null (instead of a concrete result) the validate method must propagate that null value to the caller.
A custom OutputFormat that builds a domain‑specific DTO from the validation result should have its object returned unchanged by the validate method.

The schema contains a $ref to another schema file. The referenced schema defines a required property that is missing in the provided JSON, so validation yields a message. The mock OutputFormat collects the message and returns the predefined failure value.

group: Recursive anchor does not cause infinite loop

cases.description: A schema that uses the "$recursiveAnchor": true keyword can reference itself. Validation of a JSON document that satisfies the recursive definition must complete without stack overflow, returning an empty message set that the mock OutputFormat translates to success.
If the OutputFormat implementation throws a java.lang.Error (e.g., AssertionError) the validate method must not catch it; the Error should propagate unchanged to the caller.
